title: Speed up ranked reclamation with ordered retired-register buckets
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

`joint_dual_reclaim_compiler.acquire()` sorts the complete retired-register set on every acquisition. Maintain sorted slot buckets by current frame rank instead, preserving the exact descending-rank, ascending-slot selection order. When clearing raises a retired anchor's frame, move that anchor between buckets before its next acquisition.

This addresses the compiler bottleneck identified in #154 and is independent of its concurrent-check and frame-algebra changes. No mathematical hypotheses, emitted words, profile counts, or bound change. The source manifest and derived certificate digests are regenerated through the existing authoring scripts; the complete source closure remains enforced.

On a DGX Spark with Python 3.12, the prototype reduced the two compiler runs from a mean combined 140.1 s to 44.6 s (two runs per variant and axis, reversed order). A separate full original `verify_joint_dual.py` comparison, including C++ compilation, regeneration, independent replay, profiles and composition, was 128.2 s → 49.7 s (one run per variant). That benchmark used PR165 at `7518fed2688baf25c7c32bae32674f3334b517da`; its compiler source is byte-identical to current main `d1d6c070f5a8c684727ee7ec35d930f9ebfa9758`. These timings are scoped to that verifier, not the whole repository.

Prepared by Chafik Boukhalfa with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. The PR57 compiler and existing contributor attribution are retained.

## Validation

Validated committed tree `f1081fabbfadaaaaf7292a40d428dbbb865ce920` on the Spark (Python 3.12.3):

- `make joint-dual-verify`: PASS, including the full original verifier and all 10 existing control tests.
- All 14 native `make verify-*` groups: PASS in isolated snapshots of the same source. This includes `make paired-cube-verify` and every isolated unit-test module. The tested source bytes were compared with the published commit.
- The first `verify-positive` run lacked the Boost development headers that CI installs. After supplying Ubuntu's Boost 1.83 headers in a local dependency directory, a fresh clone of the identical source passed that complete group. No source or tracked artifact changed during the rerun.
- Certificate comparison: only the compiler source hash, source-manifest hash, and derived validation-certificate hash change. All mathematical fields and both serialized words are unchanged.
- `git diff --check`: PASS.

The complete h=23 and h=25 serialized words and compiler receipts must reproduce exactly, including every input and dirty basis column in both orientations. Independent word replay, prepared transitions, original C++ CRT profiles, all 47 strict inequalities, seven margins and existing adverse controls remain enabled. The conditional bound remains `4764513337/10^14`.
